observation.visible_scene: A person in a dance studio is filmed from behind, standing on a pale floor and facing a wall-length mirror that shows their front view (wearing a pink face mask). They wear a black cutout crop top, black wide-leg pants, white sneakers, and hair in a bun with a clip. The studio has a ballet barre visible in the mirror, a row of string lights along the top, an exercise ball at the left edge, and a gray bench with a bag at the right. The camera framing and all background elements stay fixed across the clip, so the visible motion is the dancer's own, not camera movement.
visible_changes: Early frames (t≈0–0.5 s): both arms are raised at head height with hands forming a two-finger 'horns' gesture; the stance is wide with legs apart.
Mid frames (t≈0.5–1.0 s): the hands curl into fists near the shoulders and lower toward the waist, and the wide stance narrows as the body straightens.
t≈1.0–1.4 s: the dancer lifts one leg with a bent knee while one arm extends outward to the side with an open palm, then that arm returns.
t≈1.5–2.0 s: hands rest near the hips/waist with feet planted, then one arm flicks/extends outward again.
t≈2.1–2.7 s (end): one arm is raised with the hand held flat near the face/shoulder while the other hand stays on the hip; this pose is held with only small adjustments to the last frame.
Throughout, the mirror reflection reproduces every arm, hand, and leg movement in exact sync, confirming it is the same person's mirror image rather than a second dancer.
outside_clip_unknowns: This is a temporally cropped mid-routine segment; the choreography before t=0 and after t≈2.7 s is not shown, nor is any music or cue that drives the moves.
It is unknown whether the final raised-hand pose is a held position or the start of a further transition.
uncertain_details: Fine weight shifts and small body bounces are hard to resolve at this sampling rate; exact foot placement during the leg lift is unclear.
Left/right orientation of limbs is reversed in the reflection, so 'left/right' should be read relative to the dancer's own body, not the mirror image.
